title: A novel technique for simultaneous determination of drugs using magnetic nanoparticles based dispersive micro-solid-phase extraction in biological fluids and wastewaters
author: Shiri, Alizadeh, et al.

steps.title: Synthesize Fe3O4 nanoparticles
steps.instruction: Dissolve 2 g FeCl₃·6H₂O and 5.46 g FeCl₂·2H₂O in 100 mL double‑distilled water under nitrogen at 80 °C; add 10 mL dense ammonia solution and stir at 1200 rpm. After 30 min separate the black Fe₃O₄ particles with a magnet, wash repeatedly with water until pH 7, and dry in an oven at 50 °C for 24 h.

steps.title: Coat Fe3O4 with first SiO₂ layer
steps.instruction: Disperse 2 g of the dried Fe₃O₄ particles in 500 mL double‑distilled water (repeat dispersion twice) and ultrasonicate for 30 min; separate the particles magnetically and stir them in 2 N ammonia solution (NH₄OH, 28–30 % wt) at 80 °C for 3 h. Cool to room temperature. Prepare a solution of 3 mL TEOS (98 %) in 100 mL ethanol and add it dropwise to the suspension at 0.8 mL min⁻¹ to form a silica shell. Separate the brown Fe₃O₄@SiO₂ particles with a magnet, wash several times with ethanol and distilled water, and collect.

steps.title: Form Fe3O4@SiO2@Kit‑6 mesoporous shell
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1.25 g Pluronic P123 in 50 mL double‑distilled water; add 2 g Fe₃O₄@SiO₂ and 2.4 mL concentrated HCl (37 %) while stirring mechanically at 1200 rpm. After 24 h add 2 mL n‑butyl alcohol and 2.4 mL TEOS, then transfer the mixture to a Teflon‑lined stainless‑steel autoclave and incubate at 100 °C for 12 h. Calcine the resulting solid at 550 °C for 6 h (using ethanol/HCl as indicated). Separate the brown Fe₃O₄@SiO₂@Kit‑6 particles magnetically, wash with ethanol and water, and dry at 60 °C.

steps.title: Introduce NH₂ groups (APTMS grafting)
steps.instruction: In dry toluene, disperse 1 g Fe₃O₄@SiO₂@Kit‑6 in 50 mL dry toluene and heat to 110 °C; add 4 mL aminopropyl‑trimethoxysilane (APTMS) and reflux for 4 h in a round‑bottom flask. Filter, collect the brown Fe₃O₄@SiO₂@Kit‑6@NH₂ solid with a magnet, wash with ethanol and double‑distilled water, and dry in an oven at 70 °C.

steps.title: Prepare human serum and urine samples
steps.instruction: Collect serum or urine from healthy volunteers. To 1 mL of each sample add 3 mL acetonitrile, vortex, and centrifuge at 2000 rpm for 10 min. Collect the supernatant and dilute with double‑distilled water. For urine, further dilute with water, filter through Whatman No. 42 filter paper, and store at 4 °C in the dark. Prepare a stock solution of each analyte (IBF, FPC, MTC, CZP) at 100 mg L⁻¹ in ethanol and make working standards by dilution. Spike 10 mL of the prepared serum or urine with the desired concentration of standards before extraction.

steps.title: Perform magnetic dispersive micro‑SPE
steps.instruction: Place 10 mL of the spiked sample or aqueous standard (containing 100 µg L⁻¹ of each drug) in a tube, adjust the pH to 5, and add 25 mg of Fe₃O₄@SiO₂@Kit‑6@NH₂ nanoparticles. Vortex for 6 min to disperse the adsorbent, then collect the magnetic particles with an external magnet and decant the supernatant. Elute the adsorbed analytes by adding 30 µL methanol, vortex for 5 min to complete desorption, and again collect the particles magnetically. Withdraw approximately 1 µL of the methanol eluate and inject into the HPLC‑UV system for analysis.

steps.title: HPLC‑UV analysis of eluate
steps.instruction: Inject the 1 µL methanol eluate into the HPLC‑UV instrument; monitor the analytes at their characteristic retention times (MTC ≈ 3.2 min, FPC ≈ 5.5 min, IBF ≈ 9.8 min, CZP ≈ 15.2 min) and record peak areas for quantification.
